title: Shape the Queue
question: The roll leads with the card stream and its submit drawer. Lock one structure, steer, or re-roll. The visual world stays as it is: neutral chrome, one accent, judged against footage.

options.label: Card stream + submit drawer
options.lineage: the desk's job list as one column, with the intake beside it
options.thesis: One column of jobs, newest on top; submitting is a drawer that stays open beside it, never a form above it.
materials: a footage frame on every card
options.viewport: A full-height stream of job cards (frame, name, client, state, when) fills the page; a 320px drawer on the right holds the drop zone, language, client and Start, and stays open. Below a quiet 'Earlier' divider the stream continues as the archive, with a search field pinned at the top of the stream.
options.risk: On a laptop the drawer competes with the stream for width; below 1100px it must fold to a bar or the cards starve.

regions.label: live and recent jobs, one card each
drop zone / Browse, language, client, Start

options.label: Drop-first desk
options.lineage: the whole page as the place you drop footage
options.thesis: The page is the drop target; the queue rises beneath it and the archive folds under it.
options.viewport: A wide, shallow drop band across the top (drop files here / Browse) carrying a slim strip of language, client and Start; below it the recent jobs as frame-led cards in two columns; at the bottom 'Earlier' with its search field.
options.risk: A permanently visible drop band spends the first quarter of the viewport on an action that happens a few times a day.

regions.label: recent jobs, two columns of frame-led cards

options.label: Ledger
options.lineage: the desk's log as a table you scan, sort and search
options.thesis: Every job is a row; the desk is a table, and submit is a sticky bar above it.
materials: dense rows with a small frame
options.viewport: A sticky top bar: drop / Browse, language, client, Start (batch by nature). Below, one table: frame, file, client, language, state with progress, when, actions; live rows first, then everything, paged, with search in the table head.
options.risk: Rows flatten hierarchy: a failed job must still be the loudest thing on the page, and a table on a phone is a scroll.

regions.label: rows: frame · file · client · language · state · when · actions
